title: Data Handling: Tallies, Pictographs and Tables
seo_title: Grade 2 Data Handling Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 2: Collect, sort, represent and interpret data
standard_text: Collect and sort objects and data; represent data in pictographs and bar graphs; discuss and report on data.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 2 maths worksheets: tally charts, pictographs with a key, block graphs and tables. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Tally marks: 4 lines and a line across make 5.
  • In a pictograph, check the key: one picture may stand for 2.
  • In a block graph, count the blocks in each column.
  • Answer the question with the numbers you read.

Examples

Example

Key: 1 picture = 2 votes; 4 pictures

4 × 2

Answer: 8 votes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Tally groupsA group with a line across is 5.
The key1 picture can be 2.
The wrong columnFollow the column with your finger.

faq.a: Grade R to Grade 3 in South African schools. Learners are about 7 to 8 years old in Grade 2.
It tells what each picture stands for.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 1 group of 5. Count in 5s: 5. So it is 5.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 1 group of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7. So it is 7.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 2 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10. So it is 10.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 3 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17, 18. So it is 18.

items.q: How many children have a dog?
items.e: Find the Dog row. It has 2 groups of 5 and 1 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11. So it is 11.

items.q: How many woodlice were found?
items.e: Find the Woodlouse row. It has 1 group of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7. So it is 7.

items.q: How many black cars went past?
items.e: Find the Black row. It has 2 groups of 5 and 4 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13, 14. So it is 14.

items.q: How many children chose mint?
items.e: Find the Mint row. It has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13.

items.q: Which row shows 18 children?
items.e: 18 is 5 + 5 + 5 + 3. The Orange row has 3 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17, 18. So it is 18.

items.q: Which row shows 15 birds?
items.e: 15 is 5 + 5 + 5. The Blue tit row has 3 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. So it is 15.

items.q: Which minibeast did they find the most of?
items.e: Count every row: Spider 6, Snail 5, Ladybird 10, Woodlouse 7. The biggest number is 10, for Ladybird.

items.q: Which flavour is the least popular?
items.e: Count every row: Vanilla 7, Chocolate 17, Mint 13, Strawberry 8. The smallest number is 7, for Vanilla.

items.q: Which tally shows 8?
items.e: C is right: 1 group of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So it is 8. A: it has one mark too many; B: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6; D: it has one mark too few.

items.q: Which tally shows 13?
items.e: A is right: 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13. B: the groups have no line across, so they are hard to count in 5s; C: it has one mark too few; D: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6.

items.q: Which tally shows 17?
items.e: D is right: 3 groups of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17. So it is 17. A: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6; B: it has one mark too many; C: the groups have no line across, so they are hard to count in 5s.

items.q: How many more children have a dog than a rabbit?
items.e: Dog: 11. Rabbit: 2. How many more means find the difference: 11 − 2 = 9.

items.q: How many fewer blue cars than silver cars went past?
items.e: Silver: 18. Blue: 9. How many fewer means find the difference: 18 − 9 = 9.

items.q: How many children voted altogether?
items.e: Count every row: Grapes 14, Orange 18, Apple 10, Banana 5. Then add: 14 + 18 + 10 + 5 = 47.

items.q: How many birds were seen altogether?
items.e: Count every row: Blue tit 15, Pigeon 12, Blackbird 6, Robin 2. Then add: 15 + 12 + 6 + 2 = 35.

items.q: How many children chose mint?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. Count the circles in the Mint row: 9 children.
Each star = 1 bird. Count the stars in the Sparrow row: 7 sparrows.

items.q: How many children chose soccer?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Count the squares in the Soccer row: 6 children.
Each heart = 1 minibeast. Count the hearts in the Spider row: 7 spiders.

items.q: How many children chose oranges?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. Count the circles in the Orange row: 5 children.
Each star = 1 child. Count the stars in the Scooter row: 8 children.

items.q: Which row shows 3 cars?
items.e: Each square = 1 car. Look for the row with 3 squares. That is White.
Each heart = 1 child. Look for the row with 7 hearts. That is Dog.

items.q: Which colour is the most popular?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. The Yellow row has the most circles: 7.
Each star = 1 child. The Pear row has the most stars: 9.

items.q: Which colour is the least popular?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. The Blue row has the fewest squares: 3.
Each heart = 1 car. The White row has the fewest hearts: 2.

items.q: How many more children have a rabbit than a cat?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. Rabbit: 7. Cat: 5. How many more means find the difference: 7 − 5 = 2.

items.q: How many more children chose mint than vanilla?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Mint: 8. Vanilla: 1. How many more means find the difference: 8 − 1 = 7.
Each heart = 1 bird. Blue tit: 6. Sparrow: 8. Add them: 6 + 8 = 14.

items.q: How many children chose tag or hopscotch?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. Tag: 1. Hopscotch: 2. Add them: 1 + 2 = 3.
Each star = 1 child. Bus: 2. Car: 7. Add them: 2 + 7 = 9.

items.q: How many birds were seen altogether?
items.e: Each square = 1 bird. Count every row: Robin 9, Blackbird 7, Sparrow 6, Pigeon 4. Add them: 9 + 7 + 6 + 4 = 26.
Each heart = 1 minibeast. Count every row: Woodlouse 3, Snail 4, Ladybird 2, Worm 6. Add them: 3 + 4 + 2 + 6 = 15.

items.q: How many silver cars went past?
items.e: Each circle = 1 car. Count the circles in the Silver row: 6 cars.

items.q: How many sparrows were seen?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 birds, so half a circle = 1. The Sparrow row has 2 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4. So it is 4 sparrows.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Vanilla row has 6 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. So it is 30 children.

items.q: How many children chose apples?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Apple row has 2 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20. So it is 20 children.
Look at the key: each star = 2 cars, so half a star = 1. The Red row has 6 stars and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, then 1 more for the half. So it is 13 cars.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Skipping row has 2 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10. So it is 10 children.

items.q: How many children chose blue?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Blue row has 7 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. So it is 70 children.
Look at the key: each star = 2 children, so half a star = 1. The Scooter row has 6 stars and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, then 1 more for the half. So it is 13 children.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 children. 20 children chose tag. How many squares go in the Tag row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 steps, so draw 4 squares, not 20.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 children. 60 children walk to school. How many circles go in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 10s until you reach 60: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 circles, not 60.

items.q: How many children chose grapes?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Grapes row has 6 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. So it is 60 children.

items.q: How many children have a cat?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 2 children, so half a square = 1. The Cat row has 7 squares and half a square. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, then 1 more for the half. So it is 15 children.

items.q: Which way do the most children come to school?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 5 children. The Walk row has the most circles: 7 circles. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So it is 35 children.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 children. 7 children chose mint. What goes in the Mint row?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. That is 3 stars, which makes 6. 1 more is half of 2, so add half a star. Draw 3 and a half stars.

items.q: Which colour is the least popular?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Red row has the fewest squares: 2 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20. So it is 20 children.
Look at the key: each heart = 5 children. Hopscotch: 5 hearts = 25. Tag: 1 heart = 5. How many more means subtract: 25 − 5 = 20.

items.q: How many more children chose strawberry than vanilla?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 10 children. Strawberry: 7 circles = 70. Vanilla: 2 circles = 20. How many more means subtract: 70 − 20 = 50.

items.q: How many white and black cars went past altogether?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 2 cars, so half a square = 1. White: 11. Black: 12. Altogether means add: 11 + 12 = 23.

items.q: How many children chose skipping or hopscotch?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. Skipping: 30. Hopscotch: 20. Altogether means add: 30 + 20 = 50.
Look at the key: each heart = 5 children. Grapes: 5 hearts = 25. Banana: 1 heart = 5. How many fewer means subtract: 25 − 5 = 20.

items.q: How many children chose grapes?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 children, so half a circle = 1. The Grapes row has 5 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. So it is 10 children.

items.q: How many blue cars went past?
items.e: Each block = 1 car. Count the blocks in the Blue column: 9. The top of the column is at 9 on the scale.

items.q: How many pigeons were seen?
items.e: Each block = 1 bird. Count the blocks in the Pigeon column: 3. The top of the column is at 3 on the scale.

items.q: How many children chose vanilla?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Count the blocks in the Vanilla column: 8. The top of the column is at 8 on the scale.

items.q: Which column shows 3 days?
items.e: Each block = 1 day. The Rainy column has 3 blocks.

items.q: Which colour is the most popular?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. The tallest column is Blue: 10.

items.q: Which game is the least popular?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. The shortest column is Soccer: 2.

items.q: How many more children chose bananas than oranges?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Banana: 10. Orange: 5. How many more means find the difference: 10 − 5 = 5.

items.q: How many fewer children have a rabbit than a cat?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Cat: 11. Rabbit: 8. How many fewer means find the difference: 11 − 8 = 3.

items.q: Put the ways of coming to school in order from most to fewest.
items.e: Read each one: Scooter 3, Bike 6, Bus 12, Car 2. Biggest first: Bus (12), Bike (6), Scooter (3), Car (2).

items.q: Put the minibeasts in order from fewest to most.
items.e: Read each one: Worm 9, Ladybird 3, Spider 11, Woodlouse 8. Smallest first: Ladybird (3), Woodlouse (8), Worm (9), Spider (11).

items.q: How many blue tits were seen?
items.e: Find the Blue tit row, then read the number next to it: 8 blue tits.

items.q: How many children chose blue?
items.e: Find the Blue row, then read the number next to it: 3 children.

items.q: Which game is the most popular?
items.e: Read the table. The biggest number is Hopscotch: 16.

items.q: Put the fruits in order from most to fewest.
items.e: Read each one: Orange 9, Grapes 18, Banana 15, Pear 4. Biggest first: Grapes (18), Banana (15), Orange (9), Pear (4).

items.q: How many children are shown altogether?
items.e: Read the table. Add all the numbers: 10 + 5 + 4 + 15 = 34.

items.q: How many more spiders than snails were found?
items.e: Read the table. Spider: 16. Snail: 3. How many more means find the difference: 16 − 3 = 13.

items.q: How many children from Class 2B go to Choir?
items.e: Find the Choir row, then go across to the Class 2B column: 13. (6 is the Class 2A column.)

items.q: How many children go to Soccer altogether?
items.e: Soccer row: Class 2A 9, Class 2B 12. Altogether means add: 9 + 12 = 21.

items.q: Which colour of car went past the least?
items.e: Read the table. The smallest number is White: 5.

items.q: Put the pets in order from fewest to most.
items.e: Read each one: Dog 17, Fish 19, Cat 12, Hamster 8. Smallest first: Hamster (8), Cat (12), Dog (17), Fish (19).

items.q: How many more sunny days than rainy days were there in March?
items.e: Sunny: 12 blocks. Rainy: 8 blocks. How many more means subtract: 12 − 8 = 4.

items.q: How many days were rainy or windy?
items.e: Rainy: 8. Windy: 4. Or means put them together: 8 + 4 = 12.

items.q: March has 31 days. How many days were not sunny?
items.e: Sunny: 12. 31 − 12 = 19 days were not sunny. Check: 8 + 7 + 4 = 19.

items.q: Each child in Class 2 has one pet. How many children are in the tally chart?
items.e: Dog: 5 and 4 more = 9. Cat: 5 and 2 more = 7. Fish: 4. Rabbit: 5 and 1 more = 6. 9 + 7 + 4 + 6 = 26. (Counting each group of 5 as 4 gives 23.)

items.q: How many fewer children have a fish than a cat?
items.e: Cat: 7. Fish: 4. How many fewer means subtract: 7 − 4 = 3.

items.q: How many worms and snails were found altogether?
items.e: Each circle = 2, so half a circle = 1. Worms: 4 and a half circles = 9. Snails: 2 circles = 4. 9 + 4 = 13. (Counting the circles gives 7.)

items.q: How many more worms than spiders were found?
items.e: Worms: 9. Spiders: 1 and a half circles = 3. 9 − 3 = 6. (3 is the difference in circles, not minibeasts.)
Each star = 5. Apple 4 stars = 20, banana 3 stars = 15, grapes 6 stars = 30, orange 2 stars = 10. 20 + 15 + 30 + 10 = 75. (15 is the number of stars.)
Grapes: 6 stars = 30. Oranges: 2 stars = 10. 30 − 10 = 20. (4 is the difference in stars.)
Grapes got 30. Apple 20 + orange 10 = 30. Apple and banana make 35, banana and orange make 25.

items.q: How many sparrows were seen?
items.e: Find the Sparrow row. It has 2 groups of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12. So it is 12.

items.q: How many children chose chocolate?
items.e: Find the Chocolate row. It has 1 group of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So it is 8.

items.q: How many children come by scooter?
items.e: Find the Scooter row. It has 3 groups of 5 and 4 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17, 18, 19. So it is 19.

items.q: Which row shows 13 children?
items.e: 13 is 5 + 5 + 3. The Banana row has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13.

items.q: Which row shows 9 cars?
items.e: 9 is 5 + 4. The White row has 1 group of 5 and 4 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8, 9. So it is 9.

items.q: Which flavour is the most popular?
items.e: Count every row: Chocolate 8, Strawberry 6, Mint 18, Vanilla 5. The biggest number is 18, for Mint.

items.q: Which minibeast did they find the fewest of?
items.e: Count every row: Snail 17, Spider 5, Ladybird 6, Worm 13. The smallest number is 5, for Spider.

items.q: How many more robins than sparrows were seen?
items.e: Robin: 18. Sparrow: 12. How many more means find the difference: 18 − 12 = 6.

items.q: How many fewer children walk to school than come by scooter?
items.e: Scooter: 19. Walk: 9. How many fewer means find the difference: 19 − 9 = 10.

items.q: How many children voted altogether?
items.e: Count every row: Pear 5, Banana 13, Grapes 14, Apple 3. Then add: 5 + 13 + 14 + 3 = 35.
